summary: Missouri-born radio host Rush Limbaugh rose from DJ jobs to national conservative talk radio in 1988, spending three decades spreading racist, misogynist and anti-gay attacks and conspiracy theories that reshaped the Republican right.

evidence.note: Born in Cape Girardeau, Missouri, January 1951
Hired at KFBK Sacramento after Downey's firing; start of his right-wing persona
AIDS Update segment mocking gay men dying in the epidemic
Misogynist bits and the feminazi framing of women's groups
TV show attacks Murphy Brown over single mothers and gay characters as family values
Ailes produces the TV show, framed as a test run for Fox News
Opioid addiction, housekeeper informant in 2003, plea deal in 2006
Long run of racist on-air remarks about Black people, athletes and Africa
Courted by Bush, co-leads the 1994 Republican takeover of Congress
Racist parody song about Obama played in full, plus further slurs
Last show February 2021, death from lung cancer weeks later
Neo-Nazi podcasters mourn him as the man who made their careers possible

notes: Grandfather and father covered only as brief family background (1930s politics), so covered_span starts at Limbaugh's birth. main_span starts with the 1984 Sacramento job where his political persona began; national syndication followed in 1988. reaches_present for the post-death reactions up to release.
